01

Introduction

Data analytics is the systematic process of collecting, organizing, analyzing, and interpreting data to solve problems and generate insights that support decision-making.

This project uses the Brazilian Olist e-commerce dataset (nine source files, downloaded 6 July 2026) to analyze customer, order, payment, and geographical information. The objective is to understand the available data, identify governance requirements, and define the business problem that analytics will address. Proper data governance ensures that the data is accurate, secure, ethical, and suitable for analysis.

Tooling — all nine files were imported and analyzed in Microsoft Power BI Desktop. Power Query Editor was used to load each file, inspect data types, and run column-level profiling (Column Quality, Column Distribution, and Column Profile views); Model view was used to establish the relationships between tables that make the nine files behave as a single, queryable dataset. Screenshots of this work are included as evidence in Section 03.

03

Methodology & Evidence

All nine files were imported into Power BI Desktop via Home → Get Data → Text/CSV, then routed through Power Query Editor before any values were loaded into the report. Column Quality, Column Distribution, and Column Profile were enabled for every table to generate the inventory in Section 02, and a relational data model was built in Model view so the nine files could be queried as one integrated dataset rather than nine separate spreadsheets.

Note on scope: Power Query's interactive profiling view analyzes the loaded preview (the first 1,000 rows) by default. The completeness and row/column totals reported in the Dataset Inventory ledger above were checked against the full files; the profiling screenshots below illustrate the method and the per-column patterns observed in that preview, and the same patterns held when checked across the complete files.

  • Analysis tool — Microsoft Power BI Desktop (Power Query for ingestion, cleaning-in-progress, and profiling; Model view for relationships).
  • Coverage confirmed — all 9 source files loaded, typed, and profiled; all 9 tables joined into a single relational model, with geolocation linked in through three deduplicated bridge tables to avoid the many-to-many fan-out.
  • Known data-quality risks carried into Phase 2/3 — partial delivery timestamps in orders, sparse review text, and missing product attributes for a small share of the product catalog.
04

Business Problem Statement

The Olist e-commerce platform generates high volumes of customer, order, payment, and location data. Without proper analysis, it is difficult to identify customer purchasing patterns, understand payment preferences, evaluate shipping costs, and improve operational performance.

Objective — use data analytics to generate insights that support better business decisions, improve customer satisfaction, optimize logistics, and enhance overall business performance.

05

Data Inventory

Four datasets carry the core of the analysis: who the customer is, where they are, what they bought, and how they paid for it.

Customer Dataset

01

Identifies each customer and their general location for regional and delivery analysis.

  • customer_id
  • customer_unique_id
  • zip_code_prefix
  • city
  • state
Types — Text (IDs) · Numeric (ZIP prefix) · Categorical (city, state)

Geolocation Dataset

02

Maps ZIP code prefixes to geographic coordinates, enabling spatial and regional analysis.

  • zip_code_prefix
  • latitude
  • longitude
  • city
  • state
Types — Numeric (coordinates) · Categorical (city, state)

Order Items Dataset

03

Transactional detail for every product purchased, linking orders to products and sellers.

  • order_id
  • product_id
  • seller_id
  • shipping_deadline
  • price
Types — Text (IDs) · Date (shipping deadline) · Numeric (price)

Order Payments Dataset

04

Records how each order was paid for, including method and installment structure.

  • order_id
  • payment_type
  • installments
  • payment_value
Types — Text (ID) · Categorical (payment type) · Numeric (installments, value)

Orders Dataset

05

The transactional backbone of the platform — tracks each order's status and its purchase, approval, and delivery timestamps.

  • order_id
  • customer_id
  • order_status
  • purchase_timestamp
  • delivery_dates
Types — Text (IDs) · Categorical (order status) · Date (timestamps)

Order Reviews Dataset

06

Captures customer satisfaction through star ratings and optional written feedback for each order.

  • review_id
  • order_id
  • review_score
  • comment_title
  • comment_message
Types — Text (IDs, comments) · Numeric (score) · Date (review timestamps)

Products Dataset

07

Catalog-level detail for every product listed, including category and physical dimensions used for freight calculations.

  • product_id
  • category_name
  • weight_g
  • dimensions
  • photos_qty
Types — Text (ID) · Categorical (category) · Numeric (weight, dimensions, photo count)

Sellers Dataset

08

Identifies each seller and their base location, used to analyze fulfillment origin and regional seller distribution.

  • seller_id
  • zip_code_prefix
  • city
  • state
Types — Text (ID) · Numeric (ZIP prefix) · Categorical (city, state)

Product Category Translation

09

A lookup table mapping Portuguese product category names to their English equivalents for reporting and analysis.

  • category_name_pt
  • category_name_english
Types — Categorical (category names, both languages)
06

Privacy & Ethical Issues

Although the datasets do not contain customer names or contact details, they include location information and unique customer identifiers. These elements should be handled responsibly to protect privacy.

!

Key ethical considerations

  • Using customer data only for legitimate business purposes
  • Restricting access to sensitive datasets
  • Reporting only aggregated results instead of individual customer information
  • Preventing the identification of individual customers
07

Data Governance

Effective data governance ensures that data remains secure, accurate, and accessible throughout the analytics lifecycle.

Role-based access control

Limit dataset access to individuals whose responsibilities require it.

Encryption in storage and transit

Protect sensitive data at rest and while it moves between systems.

Audit logging

Keep a record of data access and modifications for accountability.

Defined data ownership

Assign clear ownership and responsibility for each dataset.
